recommendation: Keep this audit decision unless someone with Jira attachment access can recover Archive.zip. If recovered, compare the Patient Administration QA report entries against current build-scoped PA source and create precise follow-up fixes only for remaining substantive discrepancies.
issue_request: FHIR-17608 is a Published/Persuasive Patient Administration technical correction for FHIR-core-many. It asked editors to use attached QA review files from an earlier QA process to check whether updates had been applied; Jira records an Auto-approved resolution, applied-for version STU3, and no clarifying comments.
initial_application: No current source reference, git commit message, or pre-2026 history search result explicitly mentions FHIR-17608, GF#17608, or #17608. Historical late-2018 Patient Administration QA commits changed Account, Appointment, AppointmentResponse, Encounter, Endpoint, EpisodeOfCare, Location, Schedule, PractitionerRole references, and related source, but none is tied to the attachment or proves that every archive request is satisfied.
additional_context: Jira attachment 15604 is the apparent source of actionable details, but both secure and REST attachment-content URLs returned HTTP 403 in this environment. source/fhir.ini confirms current PA build scope for the relevant resource family, while checked-in qa/*.docx review documents are not referenced by source/fhir.ini or checked build files. Jira search shows sibling QA report issues with separate attachments/statuses, and existing combined-branch audits for FHIR-17599 and FHIR-17613 reached the same human-review conclusion for similarly inaccessible archives. Zulip and Confluence searches found no direct FHIR-17608 discussion or minutes that clarify the requested changes.
reconciliation: Created an empty human-review audit commit on the combined branch. No source files were changed because any source edit would require guessing at the contents of the inaccessible QA archive.
